_comment: Publication constants for the v0 artifact plane. Every substitutable name lives
HERE and nowhere else, so an org rename or a domain change is a one-file diff
(FS-00 §6: {ORG} and {DOMAIN} substitute mechanically). Scripts read this file;
no script hardcodes an org, a host, or a schema version.
The GitHub org name is CONFIRMED (2026-09-08): the organisation exists, and this
file is still the only place the name lives, so a rename is still a one-file diff.
Superseded wording: "The GitHub org name is proposed and pending final
confirmation."
_comment_verify: FS-00 §6.4 as amended 2026-09-01: the frozen exclusive-verify wording. The human
verify page owns the statement; machine endpoints are documented separately and
are never printed as the canonical host. Copy this string, never re-word it.
_comment_licence: D9: every covered version converts to plain Apache-2.0 on the FOURTH anniversary
of that version's publication date. index-build-lite derives each repo record's
conversionDate from the entry's license.published + this many years — the registry

_comment: FS-10 §5 (FS10-030/031/033) shields.io endpoint schema, verbatim. NOTE: the badge
body's `schemaVersion: 1` is SHIELDS' own required constant, not this plane's
artifact version, and shields validates the object it receives - so a badge carries
exactly label/message/color/cacheSeconds and never a `generatedAt`. That is the one
artifact whose body another specification owns; scripts/check-artifacts.mjs records
it as a named exception rather than a silent one.
badge.label: purpose source

_comment: FS-10 §10 is the authoritative /stats.json schema; VS-19 owns the three-state
machine and the honest-null rules. `firstDisbursementScheduledFor` is set BY HAND
here when a real date exists and is published; it is never guessed. `loi` stays
null unless URS OPEN-17 resolves public.
Every emitted artifact carries `schemaVersion` (FS-00 §6.2). These are the v0
values; the machine-readable contracts themselves are published in {ORG}/spec,
and a bump here without a matching bump there is a defect.
Dated note, 2026-09-09: `ledgerMonth`, `ledgerChain` and `ctSegment` are gone from
this list with the artifacts they versioned. The versions themselves did not change
and no published URL moved — the producer did: {ORG}/website emits `/ledger/**` and
`/ct/**` from its own sources (FS-00 §6.10). A key kept here for artifacts this
build cannot emit would be a version nobody stamps.

_comment_ledger_and_ct: MOVED, 2026-09-09 — FS-00 §6.10 and the ruling of 2026-09-07. The `ledger` block
(genesis hash, month-close offset and day) and the `ct` block (entries per segment,
genesis previous-segment hash) stood here while this repository hosted those trees.
It is canonical for registry YAML only, so both constant sets now live where the data
and its guards do: `website/src/data/data-plane.json` (keys `ledger` and `ct`, read by
`website/scripts/lib/plane.mjs` and by the ported ledger-verify / ct-verify /
ledger-append), with the prose for each in `website/src/data/ledger/README.md` and
builder reads every .json in that directory as a month file, and the guards' stray-file
rule then refuses it — the file's own comment there says so.
The values were not restated on the way out and are unchanged: the constants moved,
the rules did not. A pointer rather than a deletion because the question "where did
the month-close constant go?" has one answer, and it should be readable from the file
